<thought>We need to determine how many methyl (CH₃) groups are present in the molecule of the sample. The most direct way is to obtain the 13C NMR spectrum, which will show signals for carbon atoms. Methyl carbons typically appear in the upfield region (~10‑30 ppm). By counting the number of distinct methyl carbon signals, we can infer the number of methyl groups (assuming each methyl carbon gives a separate signal). Therefore, we will request the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
